question: During 1950–1990, India mainly exported which type of goods? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Automobiles
Primary products
Capital goods
Crude oil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Primary products

Explanation:
During 1950-1990, India's economy was predominantly agricultural, and industrialization was in its early stages. India mainly exported primary products such as tea, coffee, cotton, jute, spices, and minerals. Imports included capital goods like machinery, fertilizers, and petroleum. This trade structure was characteristic of a developing country, where raw materials were exported instead of value-added goods. After the economic reforms of 1991, India's exports diversified to include engineering goods, chemicals, and services. Therefore, the correct answer is primary products.

☛ When did economic reforms start in India? → 1991
☛ Examples of primary products are: → Tea, coffee, cotton
☛ What do capital goods include? → Machinery and equipment
☛ What is the export structure of developing countries? → Dominated by primary products

question: Which of the following indicators is NOT directly included in the calculation of the Human Development Index (HDI)? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Life expectancy at birth
Infant mortality rate
Mean years of schooling
Gross National Income per capita
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Infant mortality rate

Explanation:
The Human Development Index (HDI) is based on three dimensions: a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living. The health dimension is measured by life expectancy at birth. The knowledge dimension is measured by mean years of schooling (for adults) and expected years of schooling. The standard of living dimension is measured by Gross National Income (GNI) per capita. Infant mortality rate is not a direct component of the HDI; it is a separate health indicator that may relate to life expectancy but is not directly included in the HDI formula. Thus, infant mortality rate is the indicator not directly included in HDI.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What are the main dimensions of HDI? → Health, Education, and Standard of Living
☛ What is the health indicator in HDI? → Life expectancy at birth
☛ What are the two education indicators in HDI? → Mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling
☛ What is the standard of living indicator in HDI? → Gross National Income (GNI) per capita
☛ Which organization publishes the HDI? → UNDP
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा संकेतक मानव विकास सूचकांक (HDI) की गणना में सीधे शामिल नहीं है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)

शिशु मृत्यु दर
स्कूली शिक्षा के औसत वर्ष
प्रति व्यक्ति सकल राष्ट्रीय आय
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है शिशु मृत्यु दर

Explanation:
मानव विकास सूचकांक (HDI) तीन आयामों पर आधारित है: लंबा और स्वस्थ जीवन, ज्ञान, और सम्मानजनक जीवन स्तर। लंबे और स्वस्थ जीवन का माप जन्म के समय जीवन प्रत्याशा से किया जाता है। ज्ञान का माप स्कूली शिक्षा के औसत वर्ष (वयस्कों के लिए) और अपेक्षित स्कूली वर्षों से किया जाता है। सम्मानजनक जीवन स्तर का माप प्रति व्यक्ति सकल राष्ट्रीय आय (GNI) से किया जाता है। शिशु मृत्यु दर HDI का प्रत्यक्ष घटक नहीं है; यह एक अलग स्वास्थ्य संकेतक है जो जीवन प्रत्याशा से संबंधित हो सकता है लेकिन सीधे HDI सूत्र में शामिल नहीं है। इसलिए शिशु मृत्यु दर HDI में शामिल नहीं है।

question: Which of the following sectors has been classified as infrastructure by the Government of India for improved financing access? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Warehousing
Education
Apparel
Retail
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Warehousing

Explanation:
The Government of India has classified the warehousing sector as infrastructure for improved financing access. This designation enables warehousing projects to obtain easier loans and investments. The move aims to enhance storage capacity for agricultural produce and reduce post-harvest losses. Sectors such as education, apparel, and retail have not been classified as infrastructure. Including warehousing will boost the development of cold storages, godowns, and silos, benefiting farmers and strengthening food security. The classification was announced by the Ministry of Finance to support the agricultural supply chain and attract private investment in storage facilities.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which sector got infrastructure status in India? → Warehousing
☛ Purpose of giving infrastructure status to warehousing? → Improve storage of agricultural produce
☛ Benefit of infrastructure status? → Easier financing and investment
☛ Examples of warehousing infrastructure? → Cold storage, godowns, silos
☛ Ministry that classified warehousing as infrastructure? → Ministry of Finance

question: Which of the following sectors contributed significantly to India’s GDP growth after the 1991 reforms? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Agriculture
Public sector enterprises
Services sector
Cottage industries
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Services sector

Explanation:
After the 1991 economic reforms, India's services sector contributed the most to GDP growth. The reforms, which included liberalization, privatization, and globalization, led to rapid expansion of sectors like IT, telecommunications, banking, and financial services. The services sector now accounts for over 50% of India's GDP, while agriculture and manufacturing have seen a relative decline. This growth was driven by urbanization, expansion of the middle class, and foreign investment. Public sector enterprises and cottage industries had limited contribution.

question: Which sector was the dominant contributor to India's GDP immediately after independence in 1947? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Foreign trade
Services
Industrial
Agriculture
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agriculture

Explanation:
At the time of independence in 1947, India's economy was predominantly agricultural. The agriculture sector contributed more than 50% to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The majority of the population lived in villages and depended on agriculture for livelihood. The industrial and services sectors were underdeveloped due to lack of industrialization during British rule. The industrial sector contributed only about 10-15% to GDP, while the services sector had a similar or smaller share. Foreign trade was negligible. Therefore, immediately after independence, agriculture was the dominant contributor to India's GDP.

☛ Mainstay of Indian economy post-independence → agriculture
☛ Industrial sector's GDP contribution in 1947 → 10-15%
☛ Percentage of population dependent on agriculture in 1947 → around 70-80%
☛ Primary focus of India's first Five-Year Plan → agriculture sector

question: In which year was the Industrial Policy Resolution that gave importance to the public sector adopted?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: 1951
1956
1947
1991
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1956

Explanation:
The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 was adopted by the Government of India, giving public sector a dominant role in the economy and laying the foundation of a mixed economy. It classified industries into three categories: Schedule A (exclusive government), Schedule B (both government and private), and Schedule C (exclusive private). This policy aligned with the Second Five-Year Plan and promoted a socialist framework. It strengthened government control over heavy industries, infrastructure, and strategic sectors, aiming for self-reliance and rapid industrialization.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the first Industrial Policy Resolution adopted? → 1948
☛ What were the main reforms of the 1991 Industrial Policy? → Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization
☛ How many categories of industries were in the 1956 resolution? → Three
☛ Which Five-Year Plan was associated with the 1956 policy? → Second Five-Year Plan
☛ Which policy prioritized the public sector? → Industrial Policy Resolution 1956

question: Which of the following factors DOES NOT directly influence population distribution in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Official language
Climate
Soil fertility
Topography
solution:

Explanation:

Fertile soil supports agriculture, leading to dense settlements. Flat terrain is suitable for transportation and habitation. It pertains to language policy rather than physical reasons for settlement. Hence, official language does not directly influence population distribution in India.

question: Which of the following Five-Year Plans was based on the Harrod-Domar Model? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: First
Third
Fifth
Seventh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is First

Explanation:
India's First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) was based on the Harrod-Domar Model. This model explains economic growth in terms of savings rate and capital-output ratio. Its main objective was to boost income growth through development of agriculture, energy, and infrastructure. The target growth rate was 2.1%, but the actual achieved rate was 3.6%. The Harrod-Domar model emphasized investment and savings, forming the basis for India's early development strategy.

question_hi: भारत में पर्यटन किस प्रकार की आर्थिक गतिविधि में योगदान करता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 3)

question: Centralised planning influenced India's industrial strategy for decades. Under which five-year plan were small-scale industries given specific protection and incentives?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 3)

Fourth Plan
Second Plan
Third Plan

Explanation:

question: A primary goal of LPG reforms was macroeconomic stabilisation. Which indicator improved significantly post-1991 reforms?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Revenue deficit
Foreign exchange reserves
Fiscal deficit
Rural unemployment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Foreign exchange reserves

Explanation:
A primary goal of the 1991 LPG reforms (Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization) was to achieve macroeconomic stabilization. Following these reforms, foreign exchange reserves improved significantly. In 1991, India's foreign exchange reserves were only about 5.8 billion dollars, which increased to over 38 billion dollars by 2000. This growth was driven by export promotion, increased foreign direct investment, and a competitive exchange rate. Revenue deficit and fiscal deficit did not improve; in fact, they worsened. Rural unemployment also did not see any significant improvement. Thus, foreign exchange reserves are the indicator that was most positively impacted by the reforms.

question: What was a major challenge faced by the Indian manufacturing sector after liberalisation? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Increased competition from cheaper imports
High industrial licensing fees
Shortage of raw materials
Decline in capital inflow
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Increased competition from cheaper imports

Explanation:
After the 1991 liberalisation, the Indian manufacturing sector faced a major challenge of increased competition from cheaper imports. The reduction in import tariffs and the abolition of the industrial licensing system allowed foreign companies to easily enter the Indian market. Domestic industries had to compete with affordable and quality products from abroad. Sectors like electronics, textiles, and consumer goods were particularly affected. However, in the long run, this forced Indian industries to become competitive and improve efficiency. Liberalisation eliminated industrial licensing, so high licensing fees were not a challenge. Shortage of raw materials and decline in capital inflow were also not the main issues as foreign investment increased.

☛ What was the long-term impact of liberalisation on manufacturing? → Increased competition and efficiency

question: What is the most direct impact of poor infrastructure on rural education? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which tax was introduced in July 2017 to replace multiple indirect taxes in India as part of fiscal reforms?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Income Tax
Excise Duty
GST
Sales Tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GST

Explanation:
In July 2017, India introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST), a landmark fiscal reform that replaced multiple indirect taxes levied by the central and state governments, such as excise duty, service tax, VAT, entry tax, and others. GST is a unified tax system applicable across the entire country, based on the principle of One Nation, One Tax. It was implemented through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act and is considered one of the biggest tax reforms in India's history. GST comprises CGST, SGST, and IGST. This tax simplified compliance, increased efficiency in the supply chain, and promoted a common national market.

question: Which of the following sectors was the primary focus of India's First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Industry and Infrastructure
Defence and Security
Services and Education
Agriculture and Irrigation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agriculture and Irrigation

Explanation:
The primary focus of India's First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was Agriculture and Irrigation. The plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model, but it emphasized agriculture because the country faced a severe food shortage after independence. The main objectives were to increase food production, reduce import dependence, and develop basic infrastructure. Under this plan, multi-purpose river valley projects like Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, and Damodar Valley were initiated. Nearly 37% of the total plan expenditure was allocated to agriculture and irrigation. The success of this plan led to increased food grain production and laid the groundwork for the Green Revolution in India.

question: Rapid industrialisation was a hallmark of India's early planning efforts. Which Five-Year Plan laid the foundation for India's public sector steel plants? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 1)

Fourth Plan

solution:

Explanation:
India's Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), also known as the Mahalanobis Plan, focused on rapid industrialization, especially heavy industries and steel plants. Under this plan, the foundation of India's public sector steel plants was laid with the establishment of three major steel mills: Bhilai (with Soviet assistance), Durgapur (with British assistance), and Rourkela (with German assistance). These plants became the backbone of India's industrial infrastructure. The plan prioritized heavy industries over agriculture, marking a shift towards self-reliance in industrial production.

question: Colonial economic policies created a skewed distribution of income and wealth in Indian society. Which of the following is a key indicator of income inequality in colonial India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Unequal land ownership patterns
High literacy rate among workers
Uniform wages across sectors
Equitable distribution of irrigation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Unequal land ownership patterns

Explanation:
The key indicator of income inequality in colonial India was unequal land ownership patterns. The British implemented land revenue systems like Permanent Settlement and Ryotwari, which led to land concentration in the hands of zamindars and moneylenders, while peasants were dispossessed. This created severe rural income disparity. High literacy and uniform wages were absent; literacy was extremely low, and wage gaps were wide. Irrigation distribution was also unequal, but the primary driver of income inequality was land ownership. The skewed landholding structure perpetuated poverty and social stratification.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सार्वजनिक-निजी भागीदारी (पीपीपी) की एक प्रमुख विशेषता का सबसे अच्छा वर्णन करता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: सरकार और निजी संस्थाएं कुशलतापूर्वक जिम्मेदारियों और जोखिमों को साझा करती हैं।
सार्वजनिक भागीदार पूरी तरह से एक परियोजना को वित्तपोषित करता है, जबकि निजी भागीदार को कोई जोखिम नहीं होता है।
पीपीपी का उपयोग केवल विशुद्ध रूप से सामाजिक (गैर-व्यावसायिक) परियोजनाओं के लिए किया जाता है।
केवल सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र की संस्थाएं ही पीपीपी में भाग ले सकती हैं।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सरकार और निजी संस्थाएं कुशलतापूर्वक जिम्मेदारियों और जोखिमों को साझा करती हैं।

Explanation:
सार्वजनिक-निजी भागीदारी (पीपीपी) एक ऐसा मॉडल है जिसमें सरकार और निजी क्षेत्र मिलकर किसी परियोजना को क्रियान्वित करते हैं। इसकी प्रमुख विशेषता जिम्मेदारियों और जोखिमों का साझा वितरण है, जिससे दक्षता बढ़ती है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि पीपीपी में निजी भागीदार भी जोखिम वहन करता है, इसका उपयोग व्यावसायिक और सामाजिक दोनों परियोजनाओं में होता है, और इसमें निजी संस्थाएं भी भाग ले सकती हैं।

question: The Tendulkar Committee revised India's methodology for measuring poverty. As per the Tendulkar Committee, which criterion is considered to measure poverty?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Calorie intake
Employment status
Consumption expenditure
Income
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Consumption expenditure

Explanation:
The Tendulkar Committee (2005) revised India's poverty measurement methodology. It replaced the traditional calorie intake-based poverty line with consumption expenditure as the primary criterion. According to the committee, the poverty line is determined based on the expenditure on a fixed basket of goods and services, including essential needs like health, education, and transport. The committee set different consumption expenditure thresholds for rural and urban areas. This was based on per capita monthly expenditure. The new method aimed to reflect the actual cost of living and access to basic amenities, providing a more comprehensive measure of poverty.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the Tendulkar Committee formed? → 2005
☛ Which method did the Tendulkar Committee replace? → Calorie intake-based poverty line
☛ What is the new criterion to measure poverty? → Consumption expenditure
☛ Daily consumption expenditure limit for rural areas? → About ₹27 (2011-12)
☛ Daily consumption expenditure limit for urban areas? → About ₹33 (2011-12)
question_hi: तेंदुलकर समिति ने भारत में गरीबी मापने के लिए कार्यप्रणाली को संशोधित किया। तेंदुलकर समिति के अनुसार, गरीबी मापने के लिए किस मानदंड पर विचार किया जाता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: कैलोरी सेवन
रोजगार की स्थिति
उपभोग व्यय
आय
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है उपभोग व्यय

Explanation:
तेंदुलकर समिति (2005) ने भारत में गरीबी मापने की पद्धति में बदलाव किया। इस समिति ने पारंपरिक कैलोरी सेवन आधारित गरीबी रेखा को हटाकर उपभोग व्यय को मुख्य मानदंड बनाया। समिति के अनुसार, गरीबी रेखा निर्धारित करने के लिए एक निश्चित वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की टोकरी पर होने वाले खर्च को आधार माना जाता है। इस दृष्टिकोण में स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा और परिवहन जैसी आवश्यक सेवाओं को भी शामिल किया गया। समिति ने ग्रामीण और शहरी क्षेत्रों के लिए अलग-अलग उपभोग व्यय सीमाएं निर्धारित कीं। यह प्रति व्यक्ति प्रति माह खर्च पर आधारित थी।
